title: Quentin and the Well
premise: Folklorist Cyrus Voss returns to the village of Hollowmere to record its songs and finds their childhood imaginary friend, Quentin, waiting on the porch — unchanged after twenty years. The well at the center of the village refills every generation, and each refill demands a name freely given; Cyrus's grandmother gave theirs, which is why the noises followed them for twelve years. As the night of the refill approaches, Cyrus must uncover what was invited in, who benefits from the forgetting, and whether justice can be done for those the village fed to the water. In the end, Cyrus refuses both silence and sacrifice, sings the forbidden song aloud with Quentin beside them, and lets the well take the ones who invited it in — walking out at sunrise with the truth recorded, though not unchanged.
about_author: L. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in rural communities before turning to fiction. They write horror about the debts families leave in the ground.

chapters.title: The Porch Light
chapters.summary: Cyrus Voss arrives in Hollowmere after twelve years away, telling themselves the recording project is purely professional. On the porch sits Quentin, the childhood imaginary friend, exactly as remembered. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread disguised as nostalgia.

chapters.title: Songs Sung Once
chapters.summary: Cyrus interviews villagers who will sing each song only once, refusing repeats with practiced smiles. An old woman, Maren, hums a fragment and then goes pale. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into pattern-recognition.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: In the family house, Cyrus finds their grandmother Edith's journals — pages of names crossed out, one page torn free. Quentin watches from doorways, silent. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Maren explains obliquely that the well refills every generation and 'the water remembers what it's owed.' Cyrus laughs it off, but records everything. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: rationalism as armor, already cracking.

chapters.title: Quentin Speaks
chapters.summary: Quentin finally speaks, repeating words Cyrus said as a child — including a promise made at the well's edge. He has been waiting for Cyrus to keep it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror of one's own past self.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Cyrus matches the journal's handwriting to a parish register: children's names listed by year, ending the year Cyrus was born. The last entry before the tear is a neighbor's daughter, Ivy. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: horror becoming moral outrage.

chapters.title: Village of Polite Doors
chapters.summary: Cyrus knocks on doors asking about Ivy Hale; every household closes politely. The schoolteacher, Dev, warns them off in a whisper. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: isolation, the loneliness of seeing clearly.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Noises
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: the scratching in walls, the wet footsteps, the explanations Cyrus built. Each noise now maps to something real. POV: Cyrus (memory). Emotional beat: vindication that feels like violation.

chapters.title: Dev's Debt
chapters.summary: Dev confesses his family gave a name two generations back; his grandfather prospered. He shows Cyrus where the old meeting ledger hides. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: complicity and shame.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: The ledger lists 'invitations' — names given freely, witnessed and signed, going back two centuries. Edith's signature appears beside a child's name that isn't Ivy's. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal by the dead.

chapters.title: Edith's Bargain
chapters.summary: Piecing together the journals, Cyrus learns Edith offered a name to spare Cyrus — but the well took the offer as an invitation deferred, which is why the noises followed them. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: love twisted into a debt.

chapters.title: Ivy in the Water
chapters.summary: At the well at dusk, Cyrus hears a second voice under Quentin's — small, patient, singing the song no one sings twice. It is Ivy, or what the well kept of her. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: heartbreak and resolve.

chapters.title: They Know You're Asking
chapters.summary: Villagers begin watching Cyrus's cottage. A dead bird on the step. Quentin stands guard all night, humming. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: siege mentality, loyalty to the uncanny.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying Maren admits she witnessed Edith's invitation as a girl and kept the village's silence ever since. She gives Cyrus the torn page: her own sister's name. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken.

chapters.title: The Night Before Refill
chapters.summary: Preparations consume the village — lanterns, salt, locked doors. Dev burns his copy of the ledger and begs Cyrus to leave. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: cowardice confronting its cost.

chapters.title: An Invitation Can Be Declined
chapters.summary: Quentin reveals the rule: a freely given name can be freely withdrawn, but only by the giver's blood line, sung aloud at the well before dawn. Cyrus decides to stay. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: agency seized from fear.

chapters.title: The Village Gathers
chapters.summary: At midnight the villagers assemble at the well to renew the invitations, expecting Cyrus to be the offering. They bring ropes and hymnals. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal made physical.

chapters.title: The Song No One Sings Twice
chapters.summary: Cyrus begins the forbidden song — the well's own accounting, naming every invited child. The villagers falter; the water rises black and listening. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: courage as testimony.

chapters.title: Withdrawal
chapters.summary: Cyrus speaks Edith's withdrawal and their own refusal, voiding the deferred invitation. The well turns on those whose signatures remain — the prosperous families. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terrible justice outside any law.

chapters.title: What the Water Takes
chapters.summary: The refill comes anyway, but it takes the willing and the guilty. Ivy's voice surfaces once, thanks someone, and goes quiet. Quentin begins to fade. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief braided with relief.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Dawn. The village stands emptied of its oldest names; Dev survives, changed. Cyrus records the true song, twice, and nothing happens. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: exhausted peace.

chapters.title: Twice-Sung
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Cyrus publishes the recordings. Children in Hollowmere begin inventing new imaginary friends — friendly ones. On the last page, Quentin says goodbye properly. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: inheritance rewritten, memory kept without fear.
